title: Comparative Study of Out-of-the-Box Technology for Automatic Target Detection and Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2608.17917v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automatic Target Detection and Recognition (ATD/R) is critical for military decision support and (semi-)autonomous operations. Recent advances in object detection and artificial intelligence (AI) significantly boosted the potential performance of ATD/R. However, the scarcity of publicly available military datasets limits the application of these systems. As a solution, this paper explores the use of publicly available models and civilian datasets to achieve reasonable performance in military contexts. We benchmark several state-of-the-art models, including six iterations of the YOLO series and two variations on the DETR framework, on a newly acquired military relevant dataset. This dataset features military vehicles and challenging circumstances, including various degrees of occlusions and small targets. translated_title: 开箱即用技术在自动目标检测与识别中的比较研究
translated_abstract: 自动目标检测与识别（ATD/R）对于军事决策支持和（半）自主操作至关重要。近年来，目标检测和人工智能（AI）的进步显著提升了ATD/R的潜在性能。然而，公开可用的军事数据集的稀缺限制了这些系统的应用。为解决这一问题，本文探讨了使用公开可用模型和民用数据集在军事环境中实现合理性能的可能性。我们在一个新获取的军事相关数据集上基准测试了多种最先进的模型，包括YOLO系列的六个迭代版本和DETR框架的两个变体。该数据集包含军事车辆和具有挑战性的场景，如不同程度的遮挡和小目标。每个模型的“开箱即用”版本与在VisDrone数据集上微调的版本进行了验证。该数据集包含小目标特征。
tldr: 本文通过基准测试多种公开模型（如YOLO和DETR变体）在军事数据集上的性能，证明了开箱即用技术在军事目标检测中具有实用潜力，并强调了微调对性能提升的重要性。
en_tdlr: This paper benchmarks multiple out-of-the-box models (e.g., YOLO and DETR variants) on a military dataset, demonstrating their practical potential for military target detection and highlighting the importance of fine-tuning for performance improvement.
